verdict.root_cause: shippingservice is running the wrong artifact. A platform-automation image-reference update at 20:57:11 UTC pointed shippingservice at a demo image tag whose name suffix belongs to adservice (tr_db74d42a8009) — roughly three minutes before the 21:00:15 checkoutservice alert. Log evidence confirms the running process changed character: through ~20:50 the service was handling GetQuote/ShipOrder successfully from a non-JVM binary, and from ~20:57:39 onward the only output is a repeating trio of JVM/OpenTelemetry-Java-agent startup messages recurring every ~60-65s across at least eight cycles — a Java process crash-looping, not the shipping binary (tr_ac3dce2e2fdb). With no healthy shippingservice listener, checkoutservice's ShippingService/GetQuote client calls fail immediately: every failing checkout trace terminates at that one span with no callee-side server span present, at 0.3-2.4ms, inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart and before payment/email steps are reached (tr_051f1d738d46). The error propagates up through PlaceOrder to the frontend, producing the ~27% peak error ratio on checkoutservice (tr_5c1d5fb10f7d) and the frontend/loadgenerator alerts. The absence of any shippingservice error-ratio series (tr_b5ab1a627d41) is consistent with the service emitting no span metrics at all because the intended binary is not running.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on shippingservice as the origin and on a wrong-artifact rollout as the mechanism. (1) Traces localise the fault precisely: the only ERROR-flagged span below PlaceOrder is checkoutservice's client span for ShippingService/GetQuote, with no shippingservice server span anywhere in the trace, and the same uniform shape in every failing trace; cartservice, currencyservice, productcatalogservice and frontend logic are each excluded by successful sub-2ms spans in those same failing traces (tr_051f1d738d46). (2) Changes: shippingservice is the only service in the dispatched set with any recorded change in the window, and that change is an image-reference update to a tag naming a different service (tr_db74d42a8009), while checkoutservice, cartservice, productcatalogservice and paymentservice all returned empty change logs (tr_c83c036eee47, tr_c96b0fc14826, tr_e413d51e69ef, tr_62bf5cbc327b). (3) Logs corroborate that the change took effect and broke the process: the runtime signature flips from a working request-serving binary to a Java process restarting on a ~60s cadence beginning ~28 seconds after the recorded change (tr_ac3dce2e2fdb). The fast-fail character of the client spans (single-digit ms, no timeouts) rules out dependency_latency, and nothing in the evidence points to memory, connection or thread exhaustion. The image reference is technically configuration, but the mechanism is that the running artifact is not the one that should be running — bad_deploy — so the fix is to restore the prior shippingservice image tag and let it reconcile, not to tune a value. Note that the past cart-bad-image-tag incident matched this shape and that the empty cartservice metric series here (tr_a50874c1e3a1) is a denominator-and-numerator gap, not evidence of health; traces independently show cartservice serving fine, so it should not be read as a second victim of the same pattern.
open_questions: Every change query covered only 20:50:15-21:05:15; a change landing between 20:00 and 20:50 on any service (including shippingservice) is unqueried and could mean the 20:57:11 update was itself a reaction to something earlier.

The prior image reference is recorded as unset/unknown in the change record, so the exact tag to roll back to is not established by this evidence and must be recovered from the deployment history or registry.

Why checkoutservice's error ratio peaks at only ~27% rather than approaching 100% — whether non-checkout traffic dilutes the aggregate, whether a partial rollout left some shippingservice replicas healthy, or whether GetQuote is retried successfully on some paths.
No shippingservice crash/exception text was recovered explaining why the mis-targeted image fails to start; the log result was truncated and 20:50:23-20:57:39 is entirely unobserved.

The cartservice span-metric series is missing for both numerator and denominator (tr_a50874c1e3a1) — unexplained, and unrelated to the shipping fault as far as this evidence shows; it may be an independent instrumentation gap worth its own follow-up.

Blast radius named 12 services and 4 unmeasured edges; only 5 services were dispatched on, so downstream effects on paymentservice, emailservice, adservice and others are inferred rather than measured.
Whether the platform-automation actor will re-apply the bad image on the next reconciliation — the source of the mis-targeted tag in the automation pipeline is not identified.
